newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs, Germany to initial post-WW2 pact Dec 20.
newsitem.headline: Czechs, Germany to initial post-WW2 pact Dec 20.

text.p: The Czech and German foreign ministers will initial a long-awaited declaration on post-World War Two reconciliation on December 20 at a yet to be decided venue in the Czech Republic, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Thursday.
The declaration, which took two years to negotiate, will be initialled by the Czech Republic's Josef Zieleniec and Klaus Kinkel of Germany in the first of a three-stage confirmation.

"Minister Kinkel and our minister will initial the declaration on the 20th, but it still is to be decided where. The solution will come probably today," Foreign Ministry spokesman Vit Kurfuerst told Reuters.
Kinkel will come to the Czech Republic for the ceremony.
German Chancellor Helmut Kohl is expected to visit the Czech Republic, probably on January 21 and 22, to sign the text with Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.

In early February Czech President Vaclav Havel and German President Roman Herzog are then expected to address the parliament of each other's country in ceremonies giving final approval to the declaration, a text of which was leaked to media earlier this week.
It contains mutual expressions of regret for the Nazi occupation from 1938 to 1945 and for excessive brutality during the post-war expulsion of ethnic Germans from the former Czechoslovakia.

Prague says the expulsion of 2.5 million Sudeten Germans for supporting the Nazi occupation was legal but has expressed regret that the minority was held collectively guilty, even though some Sudeten Germans remained loyal to Czechoslovakia.
The declaration has angered Sudeten groups, who have complained that it does not do enough to compensate people who lost their property in the expulsions.
Kurfuerst said that the signing ceremony would not take place in the part of the Czech lands which Germany annexed in 1938 known as the Sudetenland.
In the text, Bonn also backs Czech ambitions to join the European Union (EU) and NATO defence alliance.
